title: PISA 2022. Predictores del rendimiento en pensamiento computacional en Educación Secundaria en España
venue: RED. Revista de Educación a Distancia
extended_summary:
This paper examines which student- and school-level predictors are associated with performance in computational thinking among Spanish secondary students who participated in PISA 2022. The study is framed around a broader educational question: why there are performance differences in computational thinking, including gender gaps and differences linked to socioeconomic background, digital competence, and access to ICT resources.

No intervention was implemented. Instead, the author analyzed existing PISA 2022 data using a multilevel multiple regression model. The student-level predictors included gender, socioeconomic and cultural status, digital competence, use of ICT for coding/algorithmic activities, and availability/use of ICT at home. School-level predictors included ICT availability at school, school ownership (public/private), and school location. The sample consisted of 30,800 Spanish secondary students from 966 schools.

The results showed significant associations for most predictors: boys outperformed girls, higher socioeconomic status was associated with higher computational thinking scores, stronger digital competence predicted better performance, and more frequent ICT use for coding/algorithmic activities and greater ICT availability/use at home were also positive predictors. At the school level, greater ICT resources and private school ownership were associated with higher performance, while school location was not significant. The author concludes that strengthening students’ digital competence and improving ICT access in schools may help support computational thinking achievement, especially in public and disadvantaged schools.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational multilevel regression study using a large, nationally representative PISA sample, but it is not an intervention study and cannot establish causality. Credibility is limited to observational associations and self-/school-reported predictors.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests sizable contextual associations, but it does not test a technology intervention or estimate an actionable treatment effect. Its relevance to the requested topic is indirect because it addresses predictors of computational thinking rather than ChatGPT or LLM use in middle school mathematics achievement.

finding.finding_summary: This PISA 2022 multilevel regression studied computational thinking performance in Spanish secondary students (n=30,800; 966 schools). The outcome is not a direct middle-school math achievement intervention effect, but a descriptive predictor model showing higher computational thinking scores for boys than girls and significant positive associations with socioeconomic status, digital competence, ICT use for coding/algorithm tasks, home ICT availability, school ICT resources, and private school attendance. The model explained 22% of student-level variance and 53% of school-level variance.
finding.measure: PISA 2022 computational thinking performance scale (mathematics assessment component)
